$description: The Kwapso design language. Every value here was measured off the live kwapso.com, not invented.

color.$comment: Eight brand values. Ink and paper carry every screen; mango is the single accent; sky/forest/poppy are marks, never surfaces.

ink.use: All text, all icons, all borders. Warm near-black — never pure #000.
ink.measured: rgb(25, 24, 23) on 487 elements — the most-used value on the site

paper.use: The page. Solid — no gradients, no patterns, no ambient glow.

sand.use: The second surface. Cards, list rows, wells, inset panels sit on paper in sand.

mango.use: The accent. One per view. It means 'this is the next action'. Fill or 2px border only — never a gradient, never text.

sky.use: Informational mark. Chart series, status dot, chip. Never a section background.

forest.use: Success / positive mark. Also the scroll-to-top control on the live site.

grey.use: Disabled state and non-semantic chart series.

ink-10.use: Decorative hairline dividers and rules only. Deliberately below 3:1 — a divider is not a control, so WCAG 1.4.11 does not apply to it. Never use this to outline a control.

ink-15.use: Card and section outlines — decorative, alongside a surface-colour change that already does the work.

ink-30.use: Placeholder text and disabled glyphs. NOT for focus rings or control borders — it measures 1.95:1 and fails WCAG 1.4.11.

ink-50.use: Control borders and focus rings — anything whose visible boundary is the only thing identifying a component. 3.30:1 on paper, 3.21:1 on sand: clears WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 non-text floor on both surfaces.
ink-50.derived: Solved: 0.47 is the true minimum; 0.50 carries headroom.

ink-65.use: Muted text — hints, timestamps, captions. 5.16:1 on paper, 4.98:1 on sand: clears WCAG AA body text on both surfaces.
ink-65.derived: Solved: 0.61 is the true minimum; 0.65 carries headroom. An earlier 0.55 measured 3.83:1 on sand and failed.

mango-deep.use: Mango hover/pressed only. Not a second accent.

sky-deep.use: The INFORMATIONAL role — status dots, info banners, anything where sky carries meaning rather than decoration. Brand sky is 1.99:1 on paper: invisible as a status mark. 3.63:1 on paper, 3.31:1 on sand.
sky-deep.derived: Brand sky darkened along its own hue to the 3:1 non-text floor, plus headroom. Mirrors how warning already uses mango-deep rather than mango — a meaningful mark gets the deep variant; decoration and charts keep the brand value.

semantic.$comment: What components actually reference. Swapping a theme means remapping this block and nothing else.

dark.$comment: kwapso.com has no dark mode. This is an inversion, not an invention: ink is already a defined surface, so ink becomes the page and paper becomes the text. Mango and the marks do not shift — the accent must read identically in both.

chart.$comment: Categorical order matches the four operational profiles on score.kwapso.com. THE STROKE RULE: mango and sky are pale by design and sit at 1.43:1 and 1.99:1 on paper — as bare fills they are not identifiable, which is exactly the flaw visible in the live scorecard's radar charts. So every chart mark carries a 1px {semantic.chart-stroke} outline. The boundary, not the fill, is what makes the mark findable, and that keeps the brand palette intact instead of darkening it into something off-brand.

display.use: Display only — hero, section statements, pull quotes. Never UI, never body, never a button.
display.licence: Serrif Condensed is licensed. This repo ships no font files; self-host in the consuming app.

sans.licence: Saans is licensed (Displaay Type Foundry). This repo ships no font files; self-host in the consuming app.

mono.value: "SF Mono", ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace
mono.use: Code, keyboard keys, and figures that must align in a column.

weight.$comment: Two weights. 300 is the voice of the system; 500 is its only emphasis. There is no bold.

text.$comment: Measured off kwapso.com. Body is 14.4px/21.6px — a 0.9rem base at 1.5 leading. Display sizes carry NEGATIVE leading (0.8), which is the single most recognisable thing about the brand's typography.

2xs.use: Legal, captions in dense tables. Use sparingly.

sm.use: BODY DEFAULT. The site's most common size by a factor of ten.

base.use: Body in compact/app density, and lead-in paragraphs on web.

xl.use: H3 / card title at web density.

4xl.use: Display, hero. Serif, weight 300, negative leading.

tracking.$comment: POSITIVE tracking on headings and labels. This is deliberate and it is the opposite of the tight-tracking default most systems ship.

space.$comment: Base 20. The site's whole rhythm is 10/20/40/60/80/100/150 — a doubling scale with a 150 'section' step on top.

radius.$comment: Three curves. Nothing in between — an in-between radius is the fastest way to make a system look generated rather than designed.

border.$comment: 2px is the accent-outline weight (mango outline buttons). 1px is structural.

elevation.$comment: THE DEFINING CONSTRAINT. kwapso.com uses ZERO box-shadows across a 5,142px page. Depth is expressed by surface colour and space alone. These tokens exist so that opting out of flatness is explicit, visible in review, and countable by the cognitive-load linter.

escape-hatch.use: Overlays that must detach from the page: modal, popover, dropdown, toast. Nothing else. Every other use is a bug.

motion.$comment: One easing, one duration. Measured: 0.2s cubic-bezier(.645,.045,.355,1) on every interactive element.

layout.$comment: 950px reading column inside a 1920px frame — measured.

density.$comment: One token set, two rhythms. This is a cognitive-load control, not a style: marketing pages need air to feel considered; dense app screens need proximity so a scan is one movement instead of ten.

compact.use: Dashboards, tables, settings, chat, anything a user works in all day.

control.$comment: Measured: 44px tall, 10px/24px padding, 50px radius, weight 500. 44px is also the WCAG 2.5.5 touch target — the brand and the accessibility floor agree, so the floor is non-negotiable.

cognitive.$comment: Budgets, enforced by scripts/cognitive-load.mjs. These are the numbers the linter counts against. They are opinions with a rationale, documented in COGNITIVE-LOAD.md.
